chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, that he said:

A man from the companions of al-Rida, peace be upon him, became ill, and so he visited him and said: 'How do you find yourself?' He said: 'I met death after you.' [By that he meant what he met due to the intensity of his illness.] He said: 'How did you meet it?' He said: 'Severely painful.' He said: 'You did not meet it. You only met that which warns you about it and makes you know some of its condition. People are only two (types of) men: One who rests at death, and one from whom it is rested due to it. Thus, renew faith in Allah and in Divine Authority, and you will be one who rests.' Then the man did so. The narration is long. We took from it the spot of requirement.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the eighth Imam, Ali ibn Musa)
key_terms.مُسْتَرَّاحٌ: One from whom rest is sought (or for whom death is a relief)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of death and how does Wilayah ensure rest in the afterlife according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) reframes the companion's intense suffering not as the finality of death, but as a divine sign (*ayat*) preparing the soul for its transition. He distinguishes between the righteous, for whom death is a 'rest' (*mustarīḥ*) due to their spiritual state, and the wicked, for whom it is a 'relief' from their burdens, emphasizing that renewing faith through *Wilayah* ensures one belongs to the former category. This highlights the Shia theological view that the quality of death is directly contingent upon one's spiritual preparedness and connection to the Imams.
